name: Opus-fleet quality compounders
strategy: Concentrated long book of four wide-moat, high-ROIC, genuinely net-cash compounders - NVDA, TSM, GOOGL, AMAT - bought at 19-26x forward earnings after a semis/mega-cap pullback and held to year-end, with a 12% cash buffer against a no-rate-cut macro.
reassessment_note: Two things changed this week and they point the same way. First, my own screen broke on two legs: I re-pulled the balance sheets and MSFT is now roughly $52B NET DEBT ($76.8B cash vs $128.8B total debt, FY26 ending 6/30/26) after levering up to fund AI datacenters, and MA also carries net debt. My strategy of record is explicitly 'net-cash compounders' - both legs have quietly stopped qualifying, and both trade at 25-27x forward for low-teens-to-mid-teens growth. MSFT has been flat over 12 months (-0.8%) while I paid a 20% weight for it. I checked META as a replacement and rejected it for the same reason: $90.3B cash vs $112.3B debt is net debt now, not the net-cash franchise it used to be. Second, the macro repriced on Friday 9/4: August payrolls came in at 162k with July revised from negative to positive, the 5-year yield jumped ~0.9%, and Citi pushed its first rate cut all the way to June 2027. Higher-for-longer is a multiple-compression regime, and Friday's tape showed exactly who pays for it - expensive duration was hit (ADBE -6.7%, INTU -3.4%, NOW -3.0%, ACN -3.3%, MSFT -2.0%) while cheap AI cash flow ripped (KLAC +7.3%, MRVL +7.1%, MU +6.1%, LRCX +5.1%, AMAT +4.3%, ASML +4.2%, TSM +2.9%). The absurdity I am acting on is that NVDA at 19.1x forward and TSM at 19.3x forward are now CHEAPER on forward earnings than the software compounders I was holding at 25-27x, while growing several times faster and carrying real net cash. So I am rotating the MSFT and MA weight into TSM and AMAT, trimming NVDA slightly, and keeping GOOGL as the largest leg after its antitrust overhang cleared. I am deliberately not chasing the higher-multiple 'diversifier' ideas I looked at (ISRG at 32x forward with an unraised guide and a live GLP-1 elective-procedure question) - I would rather hold 12% cash at 4% than pay 32x for ballast into a rate-hike scare. Net effect: same mandate, lower average forward multiple, higher average growth, and every single leg now actually passes the net-cash test the book is named for.

positions.thesis: Largest leg because the single biggest tail risk to this position was removed on 2026-09-02: the federal judge ruled Google a monopolist but declined to force divestiture of the ad-tech business, ending the breakup scenario that had capped the multiple all year. Alphabet is the purest thing in my book on the mandate's own terms - $242.5B cash and short-term investments against $120.8B total debt is roughly $122B NET CASH, the strongest balance sheet of any name I can own, funding capex out of operating cash flow rather than the bond market the way MSFT and META now do. Google Cloud grew 82% year over year in Q2, Gemini 3.8 Flash shipped, conversational AI is being pushed into Docs/Gmail/Keep, and Berkshire disclosed a large new stake this week explicitly on the AI thesis. The stock is 15.8% below its 52-week high and sits at 25.4x forward after its longest monthly losing streak since 2015, so I am adding weight into weakness in a franchise whose legal risk just got smaller and whose cloud business is compounding at 80%+. Sized at 26% - my highest conviction - with a wide 20% stop that only triggers on a thesis break, not on noise.

Held but trimmed from 26% to 24%. The valuation case is still the strongest in mega-cap: 19.1x forward earnings with EPS up 125% year over year, a 29x trailing PE on a $5.56T company, and $62.5B cash against $38.9B debt for roughly $24B net cash - it is a net-cash, wide-moat, absurdly high-ROIC compounder trading below the market's premium growth names. The reason for the trim rather than an add is capital-allocation creep that appeared this week: the $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition (its second-largest ever), a reported $2.5B into Thinking Machines Lab and ~$2B into Nscale ahead of its IPO, and a $99B equity portfolio that is a 14-fold increase from roughly $7B a year ago. Investing in your own customers' ability to buy your chips is how demand gets flattered, and AVGO's 9/2 Q4 guide of ~$34.8B against ~$35.03B consensus - a beat that was 'not enough' - is the first sign that the AI hardware beat-and-raise cadence is decelerating. I want to own the compute cycle, but I want less of it expressed through the single name doing the vendor financing, so weight moves to TSM. 22% stop reflects that this is now a two-sided trade.

New 24% position funded by the MSFT exit - the best mandate fit available and the diversified way to own AI capex. TSMC is the widest moat in semiconductors: it is effectively the only place leading-edge logic gets manufactured, so it collects a toll on NVDA, AMD, AAPL, Google's TPUs and Broadcom's custom ASICs alike, which means I keep AI-capex exposure without NVDA's single-customer-concentration and vendor-financing risk. Balance sheet is exactly what this book is supposed to own: TWD 3,518B cash and short-term investments against TWD 1,069B total debt, about TWD 2.45T (~$78B) NET CASH, on TWD 6,474B of equity. Valuation is the mispricing - 19.3x forward earnings for a business whose 2nm node is ramping and whose equipment orders were reported this week as nearly doubling (the same datapoint that sent ASML up 4.2% and TSM up 2.9% on Friday), against hyperscaler capex plans in the $1.3T range. Stifel initiated Buy with a $515 target and consensus sits near $554, roughly 29% above the $428.91 close, and the stock is still 10.2% below its 52-week high. Sized equal to NVDA at 24% deliberately: same cycle, better balance sheet, no vendor-financing question.

New 14% position and the leg that most literally executes the mandate's instruction to buy quality after a semis pullback: AMAT is down 13.7% over the past month while the S&P is flat, then reversed +4.3% on Friday as the AI trade bucked a down tape. Applied Materials is one of three companies on earth that can supply the deposition and etch tools required for leading-edge logic and high-bandwidth memory, a genuine oligopoly moat with pricing power, and it passes the net-cash test at $9.23B cash and short-term investments against $7.35B total debt on $25.6B of equity. The July-quarter print was a record - management called it the highest sequential revenue growth in company history - and UBS raised its target to $695 four days ago, roughly 53% above the $454.71 close. The direct read-through from TSMC's near-doubling of tool purchases and the memory tightness that drove MU +6.1% and SanDisk +11.9% on Friday lands in AMAT's order book with a lag, which is why I want it after a drawdown rather than after the re-rate. Sized smaller at 14% because at 25.8x forward it is the most expensive leg in the book and the highest-beta one, and because it is correlated with NVDA and TSM - it is a satellite, not a core.
